title: Tooth Sampling from the Inner Pulp Chamber for Ancient DNA Extraction
author: Gunnar U Neumann
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bqebmtan

steps.title: Prepare Workstation
steps.instruction: Set up a decontaminated environment to prevent cross-contamination.

substeps.instruction: Place a sheet of aluminium foil under the hood.
Place weighing paper and drill bits on aluminium foil on a clean surface outside the hood, or inside the hood covered with aluminium foil or paper towels.
Install the air extraction unit if available to reduce airborne dust.
Prepare 2 ml Safe-Lock Biopur tubes, weighing trays/pans, labeled sample bags, paper towels, 1:10 diluted commercial bleach solution, and UV-irradiated filtered/deionised water.
Change gloves regularly, especially between different samples.

steps.title: UV Irradiate Tooth
steps.instruction: Decontaminate the tooth surface using UV radiation.

substeps.instruction: Place a sheet of aluminium foil in the UV chamber.
Place the tooth on the foil with its corresponding labeled sample bag next to it.
UV-irradiate the tooth for 15 minutes on each side.
Handle teeth individually using precision forceps to avoid direct touch.

steps.title: Prepare Collection Tube
steps.instruction: Prepare and label the tube for powder collection.

substeps.instruction: Label a new 2 ml Safe-Lock Biopur tube.
If starting a session, tare the precision scale with the tube placed in the center.
Label a new sample bag with the sample ID.
Keep tubes closed except when adding tooth powder.

steps.title: Initial Tooth Processing
steps.instruction: Transfer the tooth and check for calculus.

substeps.instruction: Remove the tooth from the UV chamber and transfer it to the aluminium foil in the hood.
Check for calculus; if present, sample the deposit following the specific calculus protocol and clean the workspace before proceeding.

steps.title: Separate Crown and Roots
steps.instruction: Cut the tooth at the cementum-enamel junction (CEJ).

substeps.instruction: Hold the crown with pliers on a weighing tray.
Use an electric drill with a diamond saw blade to cut at the CEJ.
Alternatively, fix the tooth in a foil-covered bench vice and use a manual jeweler's jigsaw.

steps.title: Clear Sawing Powder
steps.instruction: Remove contaminated sawing powder from the pulp chamber.

substeps.instruction: Gently tap the sample onto the weighing tray to remove trapped sawing powder from the pulp chamber and root canals.
Discard or set aside (clearly labeled) the sawing powder, as it may contain modern surface contamination.

steps.title: Prepare Sampling Area
steps.instruction: Set up the collection surface for the bone powder.

substeps.instruction: Set the weighing tray/pan aside.
Take a fresh piece of weighing paper and fold it mid-way to create a crease for easier powder transfer.
Place the folded paper under the area to be sampled in the inner pulp chambers.

steps.title: Drill and Collect Powder
steps.instruction: Extract powder from the inner pulp chamber and roots.

substeps.instruction: Replace the diamond circular saw blade with a diamond ball bit.
Hold the crown with pliers above the weighing paper.
Using the drill at low speed and high torque, drill from inside the pulp chamber to collect powder on the paper.
Sample from inside the roots if necessary.
For blood-borne pathogen screening, sample the surfaces of the pulp chamber rather than drilling deep into the dentine.
If dirt/soil is mixed with powder, separate them by repeatedly tipping the edges of the weighing paper and discarding dirt particles.

steps.title: Transfer and Weigh Powder
steps.instruction: Collect the powder into the tube and record the weight.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the clean bone powder into the labeled 2 ml Safe-Lock Biopur tube using the folded weighing paper as a guide.
Close the tube, wipe it with a damp paper towel, and weigh it.
If powder is statically charged, use an anti-static gun on the weighing paper and tube.
Aim for 30 mg to 50 mg of powder; store any amount over 50 mg in a separate backup tube.
Write the weight in mg on the cap and side of the tube.
Store the bone powder at -20 °C.

steps.title: Post-Sampling Documentation and Storage
steps.instruction: Document the process and store remaining tooth material.

substeps.instruction: Take photos for documentation.
Place remaining tooth parts into a new, UV-irradiated, labeled bag for future analyses (e.g., isotope studies).

steps.title: Decontaminate Workstation
steps.instruction: Clean all equipment and surfaces before processing the next sample.

substeps.instruction: Discard disposable materials including aluminium foil and plastic weighing trays/pans.
Clean surfaces and pliers with 1:10 bleach solution, then wipe with water-wet paper towels.
Use less aggressive reagents (e.g., DNA away) for electronic devices like the drill handpiece and precision balance.
Clean reusable saw blades and drill bits by incubating them in 1:10 bleach solution for at least 2 minutes.
Use a UV-irradiated and bleached toothbrush to brush saw blades.
Rinse tools with UV-irradiated water to remove bleach and let dry.
Replace drill bits after approximately 5 uses if excessive wear is observed.
